verses.text: Then Zophar the Naamathite answered:
“Should all those words go unanswered? Does talking a lot make a person right?
Do you think your bragging will shut everyone up? When you mock, won’t anyone call you out and put you to shame?
You say, ‘What I teach is pure. I’m clean in your eyes.’
If only God would speak up and answer you himself!
If only he’d show you wisdom’s secrets! True wisdom has more than one side. Get this: God is asking less of you than your wrongdoing deserves.
“Can you get to the bottom of God’s mystery? Can you find the limits of the Almighty?
They’re as high as heaven. What can you do? They’re deeper than Sheol. What can you know?
Their measure stretches farther than the earth and wider than the sea.
If he comes by, locks someone up, or calls a court to order, who can stand against him?
He knows who’s deceitful. He sees wrongdoing without having to stop and study it.
An empty-headed person will get wise when a human is born as a wild donkey’s colt.
“If you set your heart right, reach out your hands to him.
If there’s wrongdoing in your hands, get it far away from you. Don’t let wrong take up residence in your tents.
Then you’ll lift your face without a stain. You’ll stand firm, and you won’t be afraid.
You’ll forget your misery and remember it like water that’s already flowed past.
Life will be brighter than noon. Even the darkness will be like morning.
You’ll feel secure because there’s hope. You’ll look around and be able to rest in safety.
You’ll lie down, and no one will scare you. Many people will come looking for your favor.
But the eyes of the wicked will fail. They’ll have nowhere to run. Their hope will be to breathe their last.”
